blocks.text: John 5 moves from a Sabbath healing to Jesus’ response about the Father’s continuing work. The chapter then develops the relation of Son and Father through themes of life, judgment, and testimony. The statement that Jesus was “making himself equal with God” first appears as the narrator’s account of his opponents’ inference; the following speech develops the issue rather than leaving that phrase to stand alone.

Many Bibles include an explanation in John 5:3b–4 that an angel stirred the pool’s water and that the first person entering was healed. Important early witnesses do not contain this explanation, and it is widely regarded as a later addition that explains why the sick man speaks of the water being stirred in verse 7. This means the wording should be read with awareness that its place in the earliest form of the passage is disputed.
